data.why: The repo's logs/ folder ships real raw MOF CIF structures (with solvent) that are exactly the CIF upload format the GTsR page expects, so synthetic data isn't needed.

goals: Upload a raw MOF crystal structure (CIF) and visualize it in 3D before processing
Remove solvent molecules from a MOF structure using the GTsR GNN model to get a cleaned framework
Compare the removed solvent fragment (SMILES) against the cleaned framework
Check whether the cleaned (desolvated/activated) framework is predicted to be structurally stable
Download the cleaned CIF for downstream molecular simulation or high-throughput screening

review.summary: The cleaning, inspection and export workflow is captured faithfully, and the cited screens hold up. But the tree leaves out the stability-check stage that the paper and page title put at the centre, and it states the threshold step wrongly. It should be filed after adding stability as a blocked node and feature and correcting the threshold details.
